money_at_stake.rationale: The rule covers two named commodities, and both have cited, dated market sizes that clear the B10_100 floor with room to spare. The global black mass recycling market, the more directly named commodity (the rule's own text defines black mass as shredded lithium-ion battery scrap), is valued at USD 12.13 billion in 2026 (Fortune Business Insights) and separately at USD 15.5 billion for 2025 in a report naming the sector's major companies (GlobeNewswire/Reportlinker distribution). The global tungsten market, the rule's second named commodity, is valued at USD 5.78 billion in 2026. Summed, the two pools the rule's domestic-allocation mandate touches are on the order of USD 18-21 billion, comfortably inside B10_100 and nowhere near GT_100B.

public_reach.rationale: The rule mandates that US persons allocate 100% of monthly black-mass and tungsten-scrap sales to other US persons, which structurally excludes the sector's largest LISTED global names as buyers of this exact feedstock rather than routing money to them: Umicore NV (Euronext Brussels) and Glencore plc (LSE), both named as major black-mass-recycling companies, are not US persons and are the entities this rule is designed to cut off from US-origin material, the same dynamic the occurrence's own thesis describes for Chinese buyers. On the domestic beneficiary side, the one confirmed listed company independently tied to this exact rule by a primary source fetched this run is American Battery Technology Company (Nasdaq: ABAT), whose own SEC 8-K states black mass sales represent the majority of its total revenue, that substantially all of its black-mass customers were previously located outside the US in OECD countries, and names the July 30, 2026 Presidential Determination directly. ABAT is real and listed, but its Q4 FY26 revenue was $8.2 million, a small-cap scale that does not by itself pull the leg into the 60+ 'clearly reachable' range, while larger sector names identified this run (Redwood Materials, Ascend Elements, Cirba Solutions) are confirmed or reported private. Scored at 35: a real, confirmed, but small listed foothold against a domestic beneficiary pool that is mostly private and a large global listed pool the rule is actively pushing away from this feedstock.

capture_odds.rationale: A one-year, extendable domestic-sales mandate is a real, government-created supply-side edge for US buyers, exactly the dynamic the Presidential Determination language itself frames as securing supply for national defense, and ABAT's own filing confirms it is now pivoting a majority-of-revenue product line to domestic buyers under this exact rule. But the confirmed listed beneficiary's own current economics do not yet show this converting into strong captured margin: ABAT's most recent quarter still shows small absolute revenue ($8.2 million) against no cited gross margin figure this run could independently verify as elevated by the rule (the only margin figure fetched this run, from Seeking Alpha's coverage of the same quarter, cites an 15.9% gross margin, which is a thin, price-taker-range margin, not a qualification-locked one). The mechanism is a temporary allocation order, not a permanent tariff or technical barrier, and public comments are open through 2026-11-04 with no guarantee of renewal past August 2027. Scored at 42: real, dated, government-created leverage, with the confirmed listed name's own current margin not yet showing durable pricing power.

timing_fit.rationale: The rule is not a projection, it is already in force and already visible in a listed company's reported financials: it took effect 2026-08-27, and ABAT's own August 20, 2026 quarterly filing (filed one week before the effective date) already discusses the domestic-allocation pivot as current strategy tied to the Presidential Determination. That is money moving inside the window today, not merely credible. Held at 72 rather than higher because the rule's own guaranteed duration is only one year (through 2026-08-27, 2027) with BIS discretion to extend rather than a multi-year statutory commitment, and public comments remain open through 2026-11-04, so the mechanism could narrow, lapse, or be modified inside the 2-5 year horizon even though the underlying critical-minerals-security rationale, per the occurrence's own framing, looks structurally likely to recur.
